dct_description_sm: The map title is Saskatchewan. Tactile map scale. 1.8 centimetres = 100 kilometres North arrow pointing to the top of the page. Borders of the province of Saskatchewan, shown as dashed and solid lines. Lake Athabasca and Reindeer Lake, shown with a wavy symbol to indicate water. A circle and the city name to show the location of Saskatoon. A filled star and the city name to show the location of Regina. Text labels for Lake Athabasca, Reindeer Lake and Saskatchewan River. The word lake is abbreviated as L and the word river is abbreviated to R. The abbreviation "AB" to indicate the province of Alberta. The abbreviation "MB" to indicate the province of Manitoba. The abbreviation "NT" to indicate the Northwest Territories. The abbreviation "USA" to indicate the neighbouring country, the United States of America. Tactile maps are designed with Braille, large text, and raised features for visually impaired and low vision users. The Tactile Maps of Canada collection includes: (a) Maps for Education: tactile maps showing the general geography of Canada, including the Tactile Atlas of Canada (maps of the provinces and territories showing political boundaries, lakes, rivers and major cities), and the Thematic Tactile Atlas of Canada (maps showing climatic regions, relief, forest types, physiographic regions, rock types, soil types, and vegetation). (b) Maps for Mobility: to help visually impaired persons navigate spaces and routes in major cities by providing information about streets, buildings and other features of a travel route in the downtown area of a city. (c) Maps for Transportation and Tourism: to assist visually impaired persons in planning travel to new destinations in Canada, showing how to get to a city, and streets in the downtown area.
dct_title_s: Tactile Maps of Canada-Maps for Education-The Tactile Atlas of Canada-Saskatchewan
